title: Investigate and fix grace-window credit smoothing causing undercounted usage across org-route boundary
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary:

We observed a class of undercounted usage for a subset of orgs when the policy engine applies the 'grace-window credit smoothing' heuristic during route merges and short-lived route aliasing events. The symptom is customers seeing lower billed token usage (which initially looked like a billing regression in our favor) while internal enforcement counters temporarily allow higher throughput without corresponding meter increments. This leads to incorrect quota state reconciliation and exposes the platform to subtle over-provisioning risk when failover/rollout happens.

Why this matters:
- Incorrect accounting undermines billing integrity and trust for enterprise customers using Dedicated/Private modes.
- It can lead to silent quota drift and sudden throttles when reconciliation runs or when shards are rebalanced.
- Edge cases are rare but high-impact for orgs with frequent route aliasing (multi-region blue/green) and sticky burst credit behavior.

Observed behavior / Reproduction steps:
1) Create two routes A and B under same org with a short-lived alias /remap that temporarily routes some clients to B.
2) Issue a burst of requests that exercise prefix KV caching + grace-window smoothing (default smoothing enabled in 1.19+).
3) Observe enforcement logs: allowance calculation returns increased transient allowance for route B during alias window.
4) Metering stream shows fewer debit events for the org than tokens allowed (gap ~1-2% for heavy bursts, up to ~8% in pathological clockskew scenarios).
5) After alias removed or shard failover, reconciliation pass runs and either backfills usage (showing up as delayed usage) OR triggers a throttle spike when credits are exhausted.

Initial hypothesis / root cause:
- The smoothing algorithm keeps a small 'grace credit' buffer per (org, route) to reduce transient throttles from short-lived route remaps.
- When route aliases merge or when a request is routed across a shard boundary, the engine merges smoothing buffers using floating-point weights derived from elapsed micro-windows.
- We are seeing an off-by-one/integer truncation when the merged smoothing buffer is split back into per-route debit decisions. In addition, our debit emission path has a fast-path that short-circuits meter increment when the smoothing delta is below a threshold, which interacts poorly with clock skew between shards.
- Net effect: allowance was permitted for a request but the meter increment was dropped or queued but not emitted due to race with a shard-local tombstone, producing undercounting.

Logs & artifacts:
- Example enforcement trace (redacted): https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/trace/ENF-2026-03-03-923 (internal)
- Billing discrepancy dashboard (org-scoped): https://console.redwood.local/dashboards/billing/overhangs?org=acme
- Preliminary analysis doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Grace+Window+Smoothing+Investigation
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5402 (experimental smoothing metrics), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5420 (fix prototype)

Proposed solution approach:
1) Stop using floating-point weights for smoothing merges. Switch to deterministic integer-based credit math with a shared fixed base (e.g., microcredits per token) to avoid truncation errors across merges.
2) Remove the fast-path that suppresses meter emissions for tiny smoothing deltas; instead always emit a compact meter increment that can be no-op filtered downstream but guarantees accounting.
3) Add a shard-aware reconciliation step at epoch boundary that replays any buffered smoothing deltas to metering stream within a bounded window (<= 5s) to close gaps.
4) Add a metric 'smoothing_adjustments' and expose per-org histogram of adjustments for monitoring + alerting.
5) Add an integration test harness (simulated two-shard aliasing) and a load test verifying no undercount at 1e6 tokens/min.

Rollout plan:
- Implement fix behind feature flag `smoothing_deterministic_merge`.
- Ship to canary (runtime-canary pool) with additional metrics for 48 hours.
- If stable, enable for Dedicated orgs actively experiencing the issue, then global enable after 72h.
- Post-deploy: run the reconciliation job and compare pre/post smoothed adjustments to ensure delta falls to zero.

Acceptance criteria:
- No undercount gap >0.1% in the simulated aliasing test at test load.
- No regressions in request tail latency (p95/p99) and no unexpected throttles during canary.
- Reconciliation pass backfills at most 1s of delayed metering events for any normal workload (non-pathological clockskew).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Deterministic integer math increases implementation complexity and may slightly change latency when merging buffers; need perf benchmark.
- Always-emitting tiny meter increments increases metering throughput; evaluate if downstream metering pipeline needs autoscaling.
- Whether to backfill historical undercounts or treat them as tolerated transient gains for billing (recommendation: backfill only if org requests an audit).

Next steps:
- ENG: implement prototype deterministic merge + removal of fast-path (owner: Maya).
- SRE: add smoothing_adjustments metric and wire dashboard (owner: Jordan Kim).
- Billing ops: determine policy on historical backfills and customer communication (owner: Priya Rao).

2026-03-06 - Maya Singh: Reproduced locally using simulated alias harness. Confirmed that meter events are occasionally skipped during smoothing merge. Added detailed trace logs to the Confluence doc.
2026-03-08 - Jordan Kim: Instrumented 'smoothing_adjustments' metric on staging. Saw adjustment histogram with a heavy tail for synthetic test at high burst rates.
2026-03-10 - Maya Singh: Pushed prototype PR (runtime#5420). This uses integer microcredits and always emits a compact meter increment. Initial unit tests pass; running integration canary next.

2026-03-12 - Maya Singh: Canary run (canary-3) completed 12h with no undercounts observed in the smoothing histogram. CPU on metering pipeline increased ~3%; monitoring added to alert at 10% increase.
